tagline: Across Estill County to the river at Irvine.
intro: Kentucky 89 crosses Estill County from the Clark County line to the Jackson County line and meets the Kentucky River at Irvine, the county seat. The county sits at the edge of the Cumberland Plateau, with nearly 1,000 feet of relief, and its towns keep to the river bottomlands.

Iron mining and smelting began here in 1810, and the ruins of the Estill, Cottage, and Fitchburg furnaces can still be seen. Gen. Green Clay laid out Irvine on 20.5 acres of his own land in 1812. In the 19th century the Estill Springs resort, by mineral springs in Irvine, drew Henry Clay on vacation.

moments.title: Irvine Historic Business District
moments.text: Around the junction of Routes 52 and 89, the district's 28 contributing buildings include the county courthouse, the 1922 Wallace Hotel, and the Mack Theatre on Main.

moments.title: Riverview Hotel
moments.text: The three-story brick hotel on Main Street, set on a stone foundation, went up sometime between 1913 and 1918, during a spell of oil exploration.
